richOriginalMathematics: Original Grade5 U07:L04 asks pupils to SORT quadrilaterals using sides, angle sizes and the number of parallel or perpendicular pairs, then recognize possible inclusion relationships from the actual physical shapes.

Warm-up What Do You Know About Quadrilaterals? is an OPEN elicitation. A four-sided polygon can have zero, one or two parallel opposite-side pairs, and a square has four equal edges and four right angles.

Activity1 Guess Which One: partner secretly selects one of the original eight diagram quadrilaterals; the other uses YES/NO geometry attribute questions, crosses out impossible cards and defends elimination. Actual source figure drawings are teacher assessed; the final two Han/Mai figure images are not certified numerically.

Activity2 Quadrilateral Card Sort gives publisher cards, asks each student to sort once and then AGAIN with different named criteria. Parallel side counts, equal side lengths and right angles are defensible groupings, but there is no unique prescribed sequence and the source card deck is teacher-reviewed.

Existing correct Rich V2 examples of coordinate quadrilaterals remain optional extensions. Exact selected Practice checks only classroom vocabulary and bounded attributes; two independent sorts and source drawings are teacher-scored.
